Description: hdtp-gateway on one Arm EC2 instance: Ubuntu 24.04, Docker, the node and its limits sidecar built from a release tag, Caddy in front for TLS on a name in your Route 53 zone (docs/deploy.md). The first boot is deploy/cloud-init.yaml, embedded below line by line and held to that file by scripts/deploy-check.mjs.

Hostname.Description: The name other people's agents will reach this node at, inside the hosted zone below: hdtp.example.com. It becomes the node's public URL (https://<hostname>) and the name Caddy gets a certificate for.
Hostname.ConstraintDescription: a lower-case DNS name with at least one dot

HostedZoneId.Description: The Route 53 hosted zone the hostname is in. The stack writes one A record there, pointing the hostname at the instance's Elastic IP.

InstanceType.ConstraintDescription: an Arm64 (Graviton) instance type such as t4g.medium: the AMI below is arm64
InstanceType.Description: An Arm64 instance type. The first boot compiles the node (Go) and its sidecar (Rust) on the instance; that build was not measured on any size, so the default has 4 GiB of memory rather than 2.

KeyName.Description: An EC2 key pair for SSH as the user ubuntu, or empty for none. The portal is reached through an SSH tunnel, so you will want one.

SshCidr.Description: The address range allowed to SSH to the instance (port 22): your own address, as a CIDR. Ports 80 and 443 are open to everyone, as a public node needs.

Release.Description: The hdtp-gateway release tag to build: the sources are fetched at this tag from the public repository.

Ami.Description: The current Ubuntu 24.04 LTS arm64 AMI, resolved from Canonical's public SSM parameter in the region of the stack. Leave it.

Properties.GroupDescription: hdtp-gateway: 80 and 443 to everyone (Caddy, with ACME on both), 22 to SshCidr

Fn::Join: # One first boot for hdtp-gateway on a VM (docs/deploy.md). It installs Docker from Docker's own apt
# repository held to one major, makes a service user, puts the node's sources at one release tag
# under /opt/hdtp, vendors the limits sidecar's crates the way `make limitd-vendor` does (in a
# container, since the VM has no cargo), and runs the shipped compose.yaml with an override beside
# it: Caddy in front for TLS on the instance's hostname, the node told its public URL and which
# address may name a caller. The portal stays on the VM's loopback, as in compose.yaml: the login
# message says how to reach it.
# Two placeholders, Hostname and Release, each written between a dollar-brace and a brace, are
# substituted by what carries this file (deploy/aws, deploy/azure, deploy/render-cloud-init.sh).
# Nothing else here is written that way: scripts/deploy-check.mjs renders the file and refuses any
# The posture is deploy/envoy's minus two things Caddy cannot do: it forwards no caller chain (so
# a caller proves nothing on the transport and the sealed envelope is its proof, as behind any
# terminating edge), and it limits nothing per address before the node (layer 1 of
# docs/release/two-layer-limits-2026-09-28.md is Envoy's). The caller's address does reach the node:
# Caddy writes it into X-HDTP-Client-Address and the node reads that header from Caddy's address
# Docker's packages held to one major (apt_preferences(5): a version pin with a wildcard; 1001
# takes that version even over a newer one). The repository itself is added in runcmd, as
# Read by `docker compose` in /opt/hdtp for the two files below (compose interpolation).
# Merged over the node's own compose.yaml by `docker compose` (it reads compose.override.yaml
# beside compose.yaml by itself): Caddy published on 80 and 443, and the node on one private
# network with it, at fixed addresses, so that HDTP_PROXY_ADDRESS names Caddy and nothing else.
# Pinned by digest, the tag kept for the reader: `caddy:2-alpine` as resolved on
# 2026-10-09 (the multi-platform index; its images were built 2026-10-05).
# Caddy: a certificate for the hostname from Let's Encrypt or ZeroSSL (its automatic HTTPS), the
# caller's TLS ended here, each request carried to the node over TLS. The node presents its
# identities' chains, not a WebPKI certificate, so the hop is made without validation, as
# deploy/envoy's is. The caller's address goes to the node in the header it reads from this
# proxy's address; a caller's own X-Forwarded-Client-Cert is dropped, since Caddy cannot
# forward a chain, and the node must not read one the caller wrote.
# Shown at every SSH login (Ubuntu's update-motd): where the setup link is and how to open it.

Fn::Join.Fn::Sub: hdtp-gateway serves https://${Hostname} from /opt/hdtp, as the user hdtp (docs/deploy.md).

Fn::Join: First run: the node's log holds the portal's setup link. Read it:
cd /opt/hdtp && docker compose logs hdtp-gateway | grep -A2 "setup"
The portal is on this VM's loopback only. From your own machine, open an SSH tunnel
and then open the setup link, http://localhost:8080/setup?token=..., in your browser.
Until the first boot has finished building the node, the log is empty: `cloud-init status`
# Docker's apt repository, as its documentation writes it, then the engine and the compose plugin.
# A literal block, not a plain line: YAML reads a plain "Types: deb" as a mapping.
- DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin
# The service user: owns /opt/hdtp and may run docker (the docker group is root-equivalent on
# the host, which is what running the node's containers is). No password, no SSH key of its own:
# the operator logs in as the provider's user and becomes it with sudo.
# The node's sources at the release tag, beside the files written above (nothing in the tree
# has those names, so the checkout leaves them in place).

Fn::Join.Fn::Sub: - runuser -l hdtp -c 'cd /opt/hdtp && git init -q && git remote add origin https://github.com/humandelegatedtrustprotocol/hdtp-gateway.git && git fetch -q --depth 1 origin tag ${Release} && git checkout -q ${Release}'

Fn::Join: # `make limitd-vendor`, in the Rust image the Dockerfile's sidecar stage builds with: the crates
# laid out under .build/limitd-vendor, which the compose build reads as the context `limitdvendor`.

- docker run --rm -e CARGO_NET_GIT_FETCH_WITH_CLI=true -v /opt/hdtp:/src -w /src rust:1.92-alpine sh -ec 'apk add --no-cache git >/dev/null && rm -rf .build/limitd-vendor && mkdir -p .build/limitd-vendor && cargo vendor --locked --manifest-path cmd/hdtp-limitd/Cargo.toml .build/limitd-vendor/crates > .build/limitd-vendor/config.toml'
# The build and the start. Minutes: the node in Go and the sidecar in Rust are compiled here.
- runuser -l hdtp -c 'cd /opt/hdtp && docker compose build && docker compose up -d'
final_message: "hdtp-gateway: first boot finished after $UPTIME seconds. Log in and read the message of the day."

URL.Description: The node's public URL: what the certificate names, and what the Settings page shows locked

PublicIp.Description: The instance's Elastic IP, which the A record points the hostname at

Ssh.Description: SSH with the portal's loopback port tunnelled: then open the setup link from the node's log at http://localhost:8080
